Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Ground rules I set for it:

- Only tracked files count. Untracked/gitignored scratch files at the repo roots (hello32.c, gemm.c, output.log, the PDFs, notebooks) are personal working files, not legacy code - I will list them separately and you decide.
- Submodules are off-limits (andesim `include/`, vsim `external/`) - the shared ABI is pinned by both repos.
- Intentional fallbacks (like `semihost_exit.inc`) are not legacy per CLAUDE.md.

When it finishes I'll show you the confirmed delete list grouped by repo before removing anything, then delete, run the test suite to prove the change is structural-only, and commit per repo.

# ##############################################################################
# custom_master object library (compiled once, shared by all CPU targets)
# ##############################################################################
add_library(custom_master OBJECT EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL src/platform/custom_master.cpp)
target_include_directories(custom_master SYSTEM PRIVATE ${VSIM_INCLUDE_DIRS})
target_include_directories(custom_master PRIVATE
  "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}"
  "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src"
)
target_compile_options(custom_master PRIVATE ${VSIM_COMPILE_FLAGS})
target_compile_definitions(custom_master PRIVATE ${VSIM_COMPILE_DEFS})
add_dependencies(custom_master deps generate_headers)

# ##############################################################################
# Per-CPU targets
# ##############################################################################

# Wires a per-CPU executable up with the include paths, compile/link options,
# verilated CPU library, and aceasim glue. Relies on per-CPU variables set
# inside the foreach loop below (CPU_NAME, CPU_UPPER, RTL, OBJ_SC_DIR,
# _aceasim_lib, _stub_aceasim_lib).
macro(vsim_add_cpu_executable _target _source)
  add_executable(${_target} ${ARGN} ${_source})
  target_include_directories(${_target} SYSTEM PRIVATE
    ${VSIM_INCLUDE_DIRS}
    "${OBJ_SC_DIR}"
  )
  target_include_directories(${_target} PRIVATE
    "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/andesim_abi"
  )
  target_compile_options(${_target} PRIVATE ${VSIM_COMPILE_FLAGS})
  target_compile_definitions(${_target} PRIVATE
    ${VSIM_COMPILE_DEFS}
    VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}
  )
  target_link_options(${_target} PRIVATE ${VSIM_LINK_FLAGS})
  target_link_libraries(${_target} PRIVATE
    custom_master
    "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/V${RTL}__ALL.a"
    ${VSIM_DEP_LIBS}
    "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/libverilated.a"
    ${VSIM_LINK_LIBS}
  )
  if(_aceasim_lib)
    target_link_libraries(${_target} PRIVATE
      -Wl,--whole-archive
      "${_aceasim_lib}"

function(hybrid_add_test name source)

  target_include_directories(${name} PRIVATE "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/andesim_abi")
  add_dependencies(check ${name})

#ifndef MEMORY_MAP_H
#define MEMORY_MAP_H

/* RAM Bridge. Range covers QEMU `virt`-machine RAM base (0x80000000) so
 * the same ELF can be loaded at the same physical address in both halves
 * of the hybrid handoff. The cap stops below NDS_HVM_BASE (0x90000000)
 * to avoid colliding with the CPU's HVM slave port. */
#define RAM_BASE 0x0
#define RAM_END 0x8FFFFFFF

/* Hart0 ILM SLAVEPORT */
#define HART0_ILM_BASE 0xA0000000
#define HART0_ILM_END 0xA01FFFFF

/* Hart0 DLM SLAVEPORT */
#define HART0_DLM_BASE 0xA0200000
#define HART0_DLM_END 0xA03FFFFF

/* Simulation control region */
#define SIM_CONTROL_BASE 0xE0080000
#define SIM_CONTROL_END 0xE0080FFF

/* Debug Module */
#define PLDM_BASE 0xE6800000
#define PLDM_END 0xE6800FFF

/* ACM (Andes Custom Memory) region */
#define ACM0_BASE 0xC0000000
#define ACM0_END 0xC0000FFF

/* AIA Machine-Level Interrupt File */
#define MLIF_BASE 0xC4000000
#define MLIF_END 0xC40FFFFF

/* AIA Supervisor-Level/Guest Interrupt File */
#define SLIF_BASE 0xC4100000
#define SLIF_END 0xC41FFFFF

/* SMU */
#define SMU_BASE 0xF0100000
#define SMU_END 0xF01FFFFF

/* UART1 */
#define UART1_BASE 0xF0200000
#define UART1_END 0xF02FFFFF

/* UART2 */
#define UART2_BASE 0xF0300000
#define UART2_END 0xF03FFFFF

/* AX66 Alias Region to RAM Bridge */
#define RAM_ALIAS_BASE 0x800000000
#define RAM_ALIAS_END 0x87FFFFFFF

#endif /* MEMORY_MAP_H */

#!/bin/bash

# VSim Workspace Build Script
# This script builds released vsim image tar file

set -e

# arguments to docker targets
DOCKER_TARGET="$1"
if [[ ! "$DOCKER_TARGET" =~ ^(dev|runtime|bin|debug)$ ]]; then
    echo "Error: Invalid argument '$1'"
    echo "Usage: $0 {dev|runtime|bin|debug}"
    echo "  dev     - Development environment"
    echo "  runtime - Runtime environment"
    echo "  bin     - Binary only"
    echo "  debug   - debug version"
    exit 1
fi

# Generate a version file
tag=$(git describe --tags --always)
echo "vsim version : " "$tag"

if [[ "$DOCKER_TARGET" == "bin" ]]; then
    podman build --build-arg VERSION="$tag" --output=type=local,dest=andescycle-bin-"$tag" .
else
    # build image using docker or podman, archive build results
    podman build --target "$DOCKER_TARGET" --build-arg VERSION="$tag" -t andescycle-"$DOCKER_TARGET":"$tag" .
    podman save localhost/andescycle-"$DOCKER_TARGET":"$tag" | gzip > andescycle-"$DOCKER_TARGET"-"$tag".tar.gz
fi


echo "✅ Build complete"

### Simulator SoC Memory Map:

Currently, this simulation focuses on CPU core, not memories or peripherals, therefore the simulation results
only reflects the cycles and signals of CPU itself.

For a simulation to run, we still need to provide memory and MMIO region, but in a simplest way as below table,
no distinction of DRAM/SRAM/ROM/DISK... since we DONT simulate memory devices' working.


| Region | Address |  Purpose |
|---------|---------|---|
| DRAM | 0x00000000-0x7fffffff | Program/data |
| HTIF | 0xe0080000-0xe0080fff | System calls |
| DMI  | 0xe6800000-0xe6800fff | Debug Module |
| Stack | 0x3000000- |  Stack space |


### CPU configuration

The current CPU configuration is under `data/configs`

### Add a CPU configuration

Here are the steps for adding a new CPU or modifying existing CPU configuration.

#### Software Data Flow

![Software Data Flow](fig/software_data_flow.svg)

http://e-andes.andestech.com/tools/release/

cd vsim/external/d45/config_tools

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F3 contract: `doctor` (read-only env-health).
#
#   1. doctor prints the four sections (artifacts / submodules / toolchain /
#      runtime) plus a Summary line; a healthy tree (no FAIL row) exits 0.
#   2. MISSING-ARTIFACT: a bogus VSIM_QEMU makes the qemu row FAIL and doctor
#      exit 1 -- the exit code is 1 iff any FAIL row.
#   3. The C++-only engines section (printed after Summary) reflects F2
#      discovery: the built-in qemu and a hermetic fake engine both appear
#      under `engines:`.
#
# Golden-free smoke test, run manually during driver development. Not wired into
# run_e2e.sh.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"

# 1. section structure + healthy exit code
out=$("$BIN" doctor 2>&1); rc=$?
for sec in artifacts submodules toolchain runtime Summary; do
  echo "$out" | grep -q "^$sec:" || fail "doctor missing '$sec:' section:"$'\n'"$out"
done
# exit code is a pure function of the FAIL count: no FAIL row => exit 0.
if echo "$out" | grep -q "0 FAIL"; then
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "doctor with no FAIL row should exit 0, got $rc"
fi

# 2. missing-artifact: a bogus qemu path -> the qemu row FAILs and doctor exits 1
out=$(VSIM_QEMU=/nonexistent/qemu-xyz "$BIN" doctor 2>&1); rc=$?
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[FAIL\] qemu" \
  || fail "bogus VSIM_QEMU should FAIL the qemu row:"$'\n'"$out"
[ "$rc" -eq 1 ] || fail "doctor should exit 1 on a FAIL row, got $rc"

# 3. engines section reflects discovery (hermetic fake engine via F2)
ENGDIR=$(mktemp -d -t andes-f3.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$ENGDIR"' EXIT
cat > "$ENGDIR/sim_fakeD" <<'OUTER'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
if [ "$1" = "--describe" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"vsim:fakeD","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker"],"roles":["standalone"],"state":["drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
  exit 0
fi
exit 1
OUTER
chmod +x "$ENGDIR/sim_fakeD"

out=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$ENGDIR" "$BIN" doctor 2>&1)
echo "$out" | grep -q "^engines:" \
  || fail "doctor missing engines section:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -qw "qemu" \
  || fail "doctor engines: built-in qemu absent:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "vsim:fakeD" \
  || fail "doctor engines: fake engine not reflected (F2):"$'\n'"$out"

ok "F3 doctor"

GOT_E=$(echo "$MEASURE" | grep -o -- "--pc-end 0x[0-9a-f]*" | awk '{print $2}')

# Oracle: the kernel's entry from nm; its return = the function's last
# instruction (single-epilogue at -O1; objdump flavors disagree on the
# `ret` vs `c.jr ra` spelling, so match by position, not mnemonic).
WANT_S=$(printf '0x%x' "0x$("$NM" "$TMP/vadd.elf" | awk '$3=="vadd_kernel"{print $1; exit}')")
WANT_E=$(printf '0x%x' "0x$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$TMP/vadd.elf" \
  | sed -n '/<vadd_kernel>:/,/^$/p' | grep -E '^[ ]+[0-9a-f]+:' \
  | tail -1 | awk '{sub(":","",$1); print $1}')")

if [ "$GOT_S" != "$WANT_S" ] || [ "$GOT_E" != "$WANT_E" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: window $GOT_S..$GOT_E, want $WANT_S..$WANT_E"
  echo "$MEASURE"
  exit 1
fi

echo "$REPORT" | grep -q "Measure all of" \
  || { echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: TL;DR carries no measure hint"; exit 1; }

# measure_loop: the loop's own first-pass window, [header, fall-through of
# the backward branch). pc-start = pc_range start; pc-end = the insn AFTER
# the branch in the disassembly (exact, works for compressed branches too).
ML=$(echo "$REPORT" | grep -m1 "^measure_loop:")
[ -n "$ML" ] \
  || { echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: no measure_loop: line"; echo "$REPORT"; exit 1; }
ML_S=$(echo "$ML" | grep -o -- "--pc-start 0x[0-9a-f]*" | awk '{print $2}')
ML_E=$(echo "$ML" | grep -o -- "--pc-end 0x[0-9a-f]*" | awk '{print $2}')

RANGE=$(echo "$REPORT" | grep -m1 "^pc_range:")
R_S=$(echo "$RANGE" | awk '{print $2}')
R_E=$(echo "$RANGE" | awk '{print $4}')
WANT_FT=$(printf '0x%x' "0x$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$TMP/vadd.elf" \
  | awk -v tail="${R_E#0x}" 'f{sub(":","",$1); print $1; exit}
                             $1 == tail":"{f=1}')")

if [ "$ML_S" != "$R_S" ] || [ "$ML_E" != "$WANT_FT" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: measure_loop $ML_S..$ML_E, want $R_S..$WANT_FT"
  echo "$ML"
  exit 1
fi

echo "PASS[hotloops_measure]: measure = $GOT_S .. $GOT_E (function), measure_loop = $ML_S .. $ML_E (first pass)"

//
// Tier-1 fixture: ra/sp/gp/tp/fp survive QEMU1 -> vsim -> QEMU2 unchanged.
// These ABI-special GPRs are never touched by other Tier-1 fixtures.
//
// Phase A (QEMU1): seed each alias with a distinct page-aligned constant.
// Phase B (vsim):  no-op.
// Phase C (QEMU2): verify; exit code = first mismatching reg num, or 0.

#include "semihost_exit.inc"

.section .text
.globl _start
_start:
    li      ra, 0x00100000
    li      sp, 0x00200000
    li      gp, 0x00300000
    li      tp, 0x00400000
    li      fp, 0x00500000           // x8

    slti   x0, x0,  0x5A0                 // QEMU1 drains, exits

    slti   x0, x0,  0x5A1                 // vsim drains, exits 200

phase_c:
    li      t0, 0x00100000
    bne     ra, t0, fail_ra
    li      t0, 0x00200000
    bne     sp, t0, fail_sp
    li      t0, 0x00300000
    bne     gp, t0, fail_gp
    li      t0, 0x00400000
    bne     tp, t0, fail_tp
    li      t0, 0x00500000
    bne     fp, t0, fail_fp
    li      a2, 0
    SEMIHOST_EXIT a2

fail_ra: li a2, 1; SEMIHOST_EXIT a2
fail_sp: li a2, 2; SEMIHOST_EXIT a2
fail_gp: li a2, 3; SEMIHOST_EXIT a2
fail_tp: li a2, 4; SEMIHOST_EXIT a2
fail_fp: li a2, 8; SEMIHOST_EXIT a2

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
# rv64 tools. The toolchain check is deferred to use-time (recursive `=` +
# $(error)), so a pure-rv32 `make rv32` -- which uses CC32/LD32 below -- needs
# only HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32, not HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN.
rv64_tc   = $(if $(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),$(TOOLCHAIN),$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
CC        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_all_fprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr rt_c_dlm_data rt_c_ilm_code
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill \
                    rt_c_hvm_data
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# Prereqs of the runtime grouped target(s) -- shared by the rv64 and rv32 rules.
RUNTIME_DEPS    := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

# --- rv32 fixtures -----------------------------------------------------------
# A small rv32 set for the arch-match path; the bulk of the fixtures stay rv64.
# Built via `make rv32` (NOT part of `all`), only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set.
# rv32_c_hello reuses rt_c_hello.c (markers are arch-neutral HINTs); rv32_spin
# reuses spin.S. The rv32 runtime comes from build/runtime/rv32 (ARCH=rv32).
TOOLCHAIN32    ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
CC32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
LD32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-ld
CFLAGS32       := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -nostdlib -static -Wall
VPLAT_CFLAGS32 := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -Wall
VPLAT_RT32_DIR := ../../build/runtime/rv32
VPLAT_RT32     := $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/crt0.o \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h

.PHONY: all clean dump rv32

all: spin.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
     hvm_readback.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# spin.elf: benign program at a mapped reset address; the engine-registration
# probe (tests/engines/probe_engine.sh, sim --probe) halts it mid-run via the
# DM. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

# Marker-drain probe fixtures: each writes a device / CSR / memory window,
# then hits the entry marker so the plugin drains. l2c_drain = the v5 L2C
# Control Register; wm_drain = a v6 mask-governed CSR; lm_drain = the ILM/DLM
# slave-port windows (LM transport F1).
l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf: %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
lm_drain.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

# LM transport (F2): reads back --ilm/--dlm content through the hart-local
# TCM view AND the slave-port aperture on the cycle engine (vplat runtime for
# the exit code).
lm_readback.elf: lm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h \
                 $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# HVM transport (F1, ROADMAP_hvm): reads back --hvm content through the
# 0x90000000 subordinate-port aperture on the cycle engine.
hvm_readback.elf: hvm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
rt_c_hvm_data.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin. Explicit rule, NOT in RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the
# pattern rule would look for a nonexistent rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same
# source, same link as the marked V fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS
# (drops the ROI marker HINTs) so pc-mode and marker-mode measure the
# same GEMM kernel.
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

# rv32 fixtures: one bare-asm (no runtime) + one C (links the rv32 runtime).
rv32: rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

rv32_spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC32) $(CFLAGS32) -c spin.S -o rv32_spin.o
	$(LD32) -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static rv32_spin.o -o $@

rv32_c_hello.elf: rt_c_hello.c $(VPLAT_RT32) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC32) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS32) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_hello.c -o $@

# rv32 runtime (grouped target): the runtime Makefile with ARCH=rv32.
$(VPLAT_RT32) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR) ARCH=rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=$(TOOLCHAIN32)

dump: spin.elf handoff_exit.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

clean:

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"

elf=$(ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf 2>/dev/null \
      || ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/*.elf 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$elf" ] || fail "no fixture ELF under tests/fixtures"

# 1. fast: --dry-run prints the full qemu command and runs nothing. Use the
#    reported arg order (flag AFTER the ELF) to lock the repro.
out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast "$elf" --dry-run 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "fast --dry-run exit $rc (should preview, not run): $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'dry-run: 1 command' \
  || fail "fast --dry-run did not print the preview banner (it executed?): $out"

  || fail "fast --dry-run missing the qemu command: $out"

  || fail "fast --dry-run missing -bios <elf>: $out"
ok "fast: --dry-run prints the full qemu command, executes nothing"

# Resolve a built vsim engine the way the driver does (VSIM_BIN_DIR env, then
# config.env), else the legacy in-tree build dir.
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  local v
  v=$(grep -oP 'VSIM_BIN_DIR=\K.*' "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1)
  [ -n "$v" ] && printf '%s\n' "$v" || printf '%s\n' "$ROOT/verilator/build"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# --dry-run applies to ALL run modes (fast, cycle, hybrid): it prints the exact
# command(s) andesim WOULD spawn, shell-quoted, and executes nothing. Regression
# guard for the bug where fast/cycle silently ignored --dry-run and ran the
# program (e.g. `run --mode fast hello.elf --dry-run` printed "hello").
#
# Layers:
#   1. fast   (always; needs only build/andesim + a fixture ELF): prints the
#      full qemu command, exit 0, executes nothing.
#   2. cycle  (needs a built vsim engine; SKIPs otherwise): the vsim standalone
#      command, exit 0, executes nothing.
#   3. hybrid (regression): still prints 2 commands.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"
elf=$(ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf 2>/dev/null \
      || ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/*.elf 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$elf" ] || fail "no fixture ELF under tests/fixtures"

# 1. fast: --dry-run prints the full qemu command and runs nothing. Use the
#    reported arg order (flag AFTER the ELF) to lock the repro.
out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast "$elf" --dry-run 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "fast --dry-run exit $rc (should preview, not run): $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'dry-run: 1 command' \
  || fail "fast --dry-run did not print the preview banner (it executed?): $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '-machine andes_ae350' \
  || fail "fast --dry-run missing the qemu command: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '-bios' \
  || fail "fast --dry-run missing -bios <elf>: $out"
ok "fast: --dry-run prints the full qemu command, executes nothing"

# Resolve a built vsim engine the way the driver does (VSIM_BIN_DIR env, then
# config.env), else the legacy in-tree build dir.
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  local v
  v=$(grep -oP 'VSIM_BIN_DIR=\K.*' "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1)
  [ -n "$v" ] && printf '%s\n' "$v" || printf '%s\n' "$ROOT/verilator/build"
}
BINDIR=$(vsim_bin_dir)
SIM=$(ls "$BINDIR"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | grep -vE '\.(json|txt)$' | head -1)
if [ -z "$SIM" ] || [ ! -x "$SIM" ]; then
  ok "SKIP cycle + hybrid --dry-run: no built vsim engine under $BINDIR (set VSIM_BIN_DIR)"
  exit 0
fi
id="vsim:$(basename "$SIM" | sed 's/^sim_//')"

# 2. cycle: standalone vsim engine, --dry-run previews its command, runs nothing.
out=$(timeout 30 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode cycle --dry-run \
      --engine "$id" "$elf" 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "cycle --dry-run exit $rc (should preview, not run): $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'dry-run: 1 command' \
  || fail "cycle --dry-run did not print the preview banner (it executed?): $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "$(basename "$SIM")" \
  || fail "cycle --dry-run missing the vsim command: $out"
ok "cycle: --dry-run prints the vsim standalone command, executes nothing"

# 3. hybrid regression: still 2 commands (probe -> stage -> inject path intact).
out=$(timeout 30 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
      --dry-run --engine "$id" "$elf" 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'dry-run: 2 command' \
  || fail "hybrid --dry-run regression: not 2 commands: $out"
ok "hybrid: --dry-run still prints 2 commands"

# Shared status printers for test scripts. Sourced (not executed).
#
#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
#
# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F2 contract: the SAME vplat_hello.elf (no rebuild) runs on `--mode fast`:
# QEMU's andes_ae350 services the UART2 stdio and the new andes_sim_control
# device at 0xe0080000 turns the guest's exit write into the QEMU process
# exit code. Also asserts a nonzero guest exit code propagates.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "driver not built: $BIN"
[ -x "$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64" ] || fail "qemu not built"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_hello.elf >/dev/null || fail "fixture build failed"

OUT=$(timeout 60 "$BIN" run --mode fast "$ELF" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from vplat' \
  || fail "fast: missing 'hello from vplat' in: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "fast: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

# Nonzero exit code must propagate (vplat_exit41.elf: main returns 41).
make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_exit41.elf >/dev/null || fail "exit41 build failed"
timeout 60 "$BIN" run --mode fast "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_exit41.elf" \
  </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
RC=$?

content.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F2 contract: engine registry + self-describe (the plugin + hot-plug query).
#
#   1. JSON parser unit tests pass.
#   2. the built-in qemu engine is always listed.
#   3. a self-describing engine in the scan dir is discovered (--describe).
#   4. its kind / vlen show in `list engines` (triggers are a hybrid-model
#      option, not an engine column).
#   5. HOT-PLUG: dropping a second engine in makes it appear with no rebuild.
#   6. SIDECAR fallback: a binary lacking --describe is read from <bin>.json.
#
# Discovery is exercised hermetically via ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR (which REPLACES
# the default verilator/build scan), so the real multi-MB sim binaries are
# never executed here.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
JSONTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-json-test"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"

# 1. JSON parser unit tests
[ -x "$JSONTEST" ] || fail "missing json unit-test binary: $JSONTEST"
"$JSONTEST" >/dev/null || fail "json unit tests failed"

=== 80-110
exit 3
OUTER
chmod +x "$ENGDIR/sim_nodesc"
cat > "$ENGDIR/sim_nodesc.json" <<'SIDE'
{"id":"vsim:sidecar","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":64,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker"],"roles":["standalone"],"state":["drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}
SIDE
out=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$ENGDIR" "$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null)
echo "$out" | grep -q "vsim:sidecar" \
  || fail "SIDECAR fallback failed (vsim:sidecar not listed):"$'\n'"$out"

# 7. (opportunistic) real default scan: if vsim is built, its sim_* binaries
# must self-describe and appear. Skipped when vsim has not been built.
if ls "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$ROOT/verilator/build}/"sim_* >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  out=$("$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null)
  echo "$out" | grep -q "^vsim:" \
    || fail "default scan discovered no real vsim engine:"$'\n'"$out"
fi

ok "F2 engine registry + self-describe"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# test_all.sh -- run the full andesim test surface. This is the entry point that
# replaced the former `andesim test` subcommand (which moved out of the binary).
#
# Phases (all run, in order, unless named explicitly):
#   unit      build/driver/andesim-*-test   the C++ driver unit tests
#   contract  tests/andes_sim/*.sh          driver feature + parity contracts
#   e2e       scripts/run_e2e.sh            hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]
#
# --dry-run prints the plan without executing (and without building). The
# contract and e2e phases need built artifacts -- run scripts/build_all.sh
# first. FILTER / MODE / JOBS pass through to scripts/run_e2e.sh unchanged.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

DRY_RUN=0
PHASES=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    unit|contract|e2e) PHASES+=("$arg") ;;
    *)
      echo "test_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      echo "usage: test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done
[ "${#PHASES[@]}" -eq 0 ] && PHASES=(unit contract e2e)

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F4 contract: HTIF file syscalls behave identically on both engines. The
# SAME vplat_file.elf creates/writes/reads/removes a host file (served by
# vsim's sim_control HTIF table and by QEMU's andes_sim_control mirror),
# prints "file io ok" and exits 0. Run in a scratch cwd; the tmp file must
# be gone afterwards (remove() worked host-side).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_file.elf"
SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
QEMU="${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$(cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR)}/qemu-system-riscv64"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"
[ -x "$QEMU" ] || fail "qemu not found (source ./setup.sh): $QEMU"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_file.elf >/dev/null || fail "fixture build failed"

run_leg() {  # LABEL CMD...
  local label="$1"; shift
  local wd out rc
  wd=$(mktemp -d)
  out=$( cd "$wd" && timeout 120 "$@" </dev/null 2>&1 ); rc=$?
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'file io ok' \
    || { rm -rf "$wd"; fail "$label: missing 'file io ok': $out"; }
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || { rm -rf "$wd"; fail "$label: exit code $rc != 0"; }
  [ ! -e "$wd/vplat_file_test.tmp" ] \
    || { rm -rf "$wd"; fail "$label: tmp file not removed"; }
  rm -rf "$wd"
  echo "[ok] $label: file io ok, clean exit, tmp removed"
}

run_leg cycle "$SIM" "$ELF"
run_leg fast "$QEMU" -machine andes_ae350 -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native -bios "$ELF"

ok "F4 vplat_file.elf HTIF file io parity (fast + cycle)"

lines: -/* SimControl write handler. Interprets writes to offset 0:
+ * SimControl HTIF frontend syscalls -- mirror of the vsim device
+ * The andesim vplat runtime does file io (fd > 2) by writing the guest
+ * physical address of an 8 x u64 "magicmem" block to offset 0x10 (one
+ * 64-bit store on rv64, or two 32-bit halves at 0x10 low / 0x14 high on
+ * rv32). magicmem[0] holds the syscall number, [1..7] the arguments; the
+ * host serves the call and the result replaces magicmem[0]. Both engines
+ * must serve the same table so ONE ELF behaves identically on the fast
+ * (QEMU) and cycle (vsim) runs -- and across a hybrid handoff.
+ * Newlib's <sys/_default_fcntl.h> uses BSD-derived O_* values that differ
+ * from the Linux ABI (O_CREAT=0x200 vs 0x40, O_TRUNC=0x400 vs 0x200, ...).
+ * Pass-through would drop O_CREAT, so a fopen("w") of a new file fails
+ * with ENOENT. Translate flag-by-flag (same table as the vsim device).
+/* NUL-terminated string from guest RAM (paths); caller g_free()s. */
+ * Store the two fields the guest-side newlib stat consumers read back
+ * into the guest's struct stat: st_mode (u32 at offset 4) and st_size
+ * (u64 at offset 16) -- the same two fields, at the same offsets, that
+ * the vsim device writes through its pico_stat view.
+static void andesim_store_guest_stat(uint64_t gpa, const struct stat *st)
+ * The HTIF syscall table. Numbers and semantics mirror the vsim device's
+ * sim_syscall_table exactly; failures return -1 (full-width, like the
+ * host calls' sign-extended returns). Buffers bounce through the host
+ * heap; guest pointers are guest-physical (the vplat runtime runs
+ * tohost word: bits 63:56 device, 55:48 cmd (both must be 0), 47:0 the
+ * guest-physical magicmem address. Read the 8 u64 block, serve the call,
+ * write the whole block back with [0] = result.
+/* rv32 issues the tohost word as two 32-bit halves (0x10 low, 0x14 high). */
+/* SimControl write handler. Offset 0 is the exit command:
*   value < 256          → raw exit code (used by vplat _exit()).
+ * Offset 0x4 is HTIF putchar; 0x10/0x14 carry the HTIF syscall command. */
+static uint64_t sim_ctrl_read(void *opaque, hwaddr offset, unsigned size)
+    return 0; /* the device is write-only, like the vsim SimControl */

cd /home/nick/work/qemu_andesim && git add hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c && git commit -q -m "hw/riscv/andes_ae350: serve the HTIF frontend syscalls in SimControl

The vplat runtime does file io (fd > 2) by writing the physical address
of an 8 x u64 magicmem block to SimControl offset 0x10; the host serves
the syscall and the result replaces magicmem[0]. The vsim (cycle) engine
has always implemented this table, but the QEMU device only handled the
exit write at offset 0 and silently dropped everything else -- so each
file-io 'call' returned its own untouched syscall number, which newlib
misread as success (open -> fd 6, read -> 17 bytes of garbage). The
andesim tests/vplat/test_vplat_f4.sh parity test failed on the fast leg
with 'FILEIO: readback mismatch (17)'.

Mirror the vsim device (src/platform/sim_control.hpp + htif/sys_call.hpp
in the hybrid_vsim repo) exactly:

- the 18-entry syscall table (gettimeofday, open, write, getcwd, lseek,
  read, flen, close, access, faccessat, fstat, fstatat, link, lstat,
  stat, openat, rename, unlink), with the newlib->Linux O_* flag
  translation (BSD-derived values: pass-through would drop O_CREAT),
- stat writeback of st_mode (u32 @4) / st_size (u64 @16), the two fields
  the guest newlib stat consumers read,
- the tohost command as one 64-bit store (rv64) or two 32-bit halves at
  0x10/0x14 (rv32),
- HTIF putchar at offset 0x4,
- access sizes widened to 1..8 and a zero-returning read handler
  (the device stays effectively write-only, like vsim's).

Validated: test_vplat_f4.sh passes on cycle + fast rv64 + fast rv32
(halves path); full andesim regression battery green (unit, contract,
plugin, vplat, e2e 51/0).

content.text:
Fixed. The bug was in QEMU, not the runtime: the vplat runtime does file io by writing a magicmem command block address to SimControl offset 0x10, but QEMU's device only implemented the exit write at offset 0 and silently dropped everything else. Each file-io "syscall" therefore returned its own untouched syscall number — newlib misread `open` returning 6 as a valid fd and `read` returning 10+10 as "17 bytes read", so the guest saw a successful read of garbage: `readback mismatch (17)`. No file was ever created on the host. vsim has always implemented the full table, which is why only the fast leg failed.

The fix (`qemu_andesim` commit `55af872290`) mirrors vsim's device exactly in `hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c`:
- the full 18-entry HTIF syscall table (open/read/write/close/lseek/stat family/unlink/rename/getcwd/gettimeofday/...), including the newlib-to-Linux `O_*` flag translation (newlib's BSD-derived `O_CREAT=0x200` would otherwise be dropped, breaking `fopen("w")`)
- stat writeback of exactly the two fields the guest reads (`st_mode` @4, `st_size` @16)
- the tohost command as one 64-bit store (rv64) or two 32-bit halves at 0x10/0x14 (rv32), plus HTIF putchar at 0x4

A small andesim commit (`875169b`) adds a guarded fast-rv32 leg to `test_vplat_f4.sh` — the two-halves protocol is a distinct device path I wrote fresh, so it now has coverage (it skips cleanly on hosts without the rv32 toolchain) — and corrects the runtime comment that pointed at a QEMU file that never existed.

Verification: `test_vplat_f4.sh` passes all three legs (cycle, fast rv64, fast rv32), and the full regression battery is green — unit 10/10, contract 26/26, plugin 9/9, vplat 10/10, e2e 51 passed / 0 failed. The whole vplat suite now passes, which it didn't before today.
